verdict.line: You lose if you facetank Thundering Smash into the double-W combo before level 6, but you win if you poke with Infected Cleaver and scale your health stacking into the 58% win rate this matchup actually carries.

brief.thesis: Volibear's only lockdown is Thundering Smash (Q), on a 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s cooldown — every second it's down, he cannot stop your trade. Mundo's Infected Cleaver deals damage based on Volibear's max health and gets thrown from 975 range, so you can poke him for free in every window his Q is on cooldown. That asymmetry, plus Mundo's health-stacking build outscaling Volibear's on-hit damage late, is why this sits at 58% win rate over 286 games despite being labeled an 'even' lane.

theirWindow.when: Volibear's Q off cooldown, closing distance
theirWindow.what: He gains speed toward you and the first enemy he hits gets stunned and damaged — if that lands, he immediately follows with Frenzied Maul (W) and the recast on the same target for bonus damage and a heal. Don't stand still inside his dash range; back off or juke the approach rather than trading through it.

yourWindow.when: right after his Q whiffs or lands
yourWindow.what: His stun is gone for 10-12 seconds, so throw Infected Cleaver (Q) at max range — it hits for a percentage of his max health regardless of how tanky he builds — then step in and trade autos while Burning Agony (W) ticks nearby. Without the stun he has no way to lock you into the W-W combo, so this is where you win the exchange outright.

start.why: Blocks the poke-heavy early autos Volibear uses to set up Frenzied Maul stacks, and the passive sustain lets you hold trades until your Q is off cooldown again (52.6% win rate over 213 games).

boots.why: The extra move speed lets you juke the Thundering Smash approach instead of eating the stun outright, which is the single biggest swing in this lane (57.2% win rate over 187 games).

core.why: Converts stacked bonus health into raw stats and scales your Cleaver damage as your max HP climbs — highest-performing path in the data at 73.3% over 30 games.
Pure max-health scaling that directly inflates Infected Cleaver's percent-health damage while giving you the HP buffer to outlast his on-hit poke.
Healing amp stacks with Adrenaline Rush and Burning Agony's self-damage upkeep, letting you win extended trades Volibear can't match without sustain of his own.

situational.when: he rushes on-hit or attack speed items to snowball Frenzied Maul stacks
his auto-attack and on-hit damage output is outpacing your healing
the lane is won and you want more wave clear and split-push pressure

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards the max-health poke-and-trade pattern this matchup is built around, and the healing proc keeps you ahead on sustain through every exchange (58.9% win rate, most-picked page).

summoners.why: Ghost lets you close distance or disengage from the Thundering Smash approach without eating the stun, while Teleport resets you into lane after trades and backs your scaling health-stacking build (56.6% win rate, 45% pick rate — the top combo in this matchup).

playing.title: Throw Cleaver only off cooldown windows
playing.detail: The instant Thundering Smash (Q) is used or whiffs, Volibear has nothing to stop you — fire Infected Cleaver at 975 range immediately since it scales off his max health regardless of his build.

playing.title: Never stand still in his dash lane
playing.detail: Thundering Smash only stuns the first enemy he hits while charging — sidestep the approach rather than trading through it, since getting hit opens the door to his W-W combo.

playing.title: Respect the double-W, not the first one
playing.detail: Frenzied Maul's first hit is cheap, but the recast on the same target deals bonus damage and heals him — disengage after the first W lands instead of trading through the second.

playing.title: Burn W when stunned, not before
playing.detail: Burning Agony drains your own health to shorten disable duration — save that drain for the moment you're actually stunned so you escape the follow-up combo faster, not as a constant poke tool.

playing.title: Save Sadism for sustained skirmishes
playing.detail: Sadism's movement speed and regen ramp up over time rather than giving instant mitigation, so pop it when you're committing to an extended fight, not as a panic button against a single stun.

playing.title: Scale through items before all-inning
playing.detail: Your 58% win rate comes from the mid-game onward as Heartsteel and Warmog's Armor inflate both your HP pool and Cleaver's damage — avoid forcing all-ins before level 6 when Volibear's solo-kill risk is highest.

playing.title: Track his 160-second ultimate on dives
playing.detail: Stormbringer disables nearby towers on landing and only comes off cooldown roughly every 110-160 seconds depending on rank — watch for it before committing to a tower dive or deep trade near your plates.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, boots, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.20.1); the tactical reasoning about Thundering Smash timing, the Frenzied Maul double-cast, and when to use Burning Agony or Sadism is this brief's own read on the ability kits, not sourced from OP.GG.

stats.opponentTip: Hit Volibear with [Q] when he charges in using (Q) and fight him once his (Q) is deactivated. Keep in mind that his second (W) deals additional damage!
